## Hands-on 5 – The preregistration {#the-preregistration-moment .smaller}

::: {.big}
- Aim 2: assess the **robustness** of the constrained result
:::

::: {.none}
1. Open the preregistration block in your report
2. Complete fields 1–5: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, your one specification, the one-sentence justification from your DAG, and your rule for what supports or undermines the claim
3. **Render**, or in the webR workspace copy the completed cell into your notes
4. Only then run your specification
:::

::: {.fragment}
Nothing runs until your block is complete.
:::

::: notes
Your second aim as the sixth analyst is to assess the robustness of the constrained result. In Task 4 you explored, and now you preregister one specification, with identical code; the difference is that an exploratory specification can be chosen because of its result and a preregistered one cannot. Open Task 5 and fill in the five fields, among them the data-in-hand statement, which records what you already know about the data, and the rule for what would support the claim and what would undermine it, written before any result. Then render the report, since the rendered file with its timestamp is the dated record of your preregistration; in the webR workspace, copy the completed cell into your notes. A specification already tried in Task 4 is allowed, but say so in the block. [advance] You run nothing before that record exists.
:::

## Hands-on 5 – The preregistered run {#run-it-then-watch-the-chart .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Task 5** – run the specification in your preregistration, and only that one
- `report_result()` prints a one-click link to the Google Form with your results already in it – click, submit
- Your dot joins the **Class results** page as a *declared* result (the name that the chart gives to a preregistered specification), beside the exploratory ones from Task 4
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Compare the two waves. If the preregistered dots fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, it is worth discussing why.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Stuck? Raise your hand; reload and rerun; try a second browser; follow my screen; as a last resort, your specification is one row of the curve, which the download button on the Specification curve page serves with its *t* and df
:::

::: notes
Go. Run the specification of your preregistration, and only that one, and once the numbers are in front of you, call `report_result()`, which prints a link to the form with your values already filled in. Your dot joins the chart as a declared result, the name that the chart gives to a preregistered specification, beside the exploratory dots submitted in Task 4. [advance] If the declared dots fall systematically to one side of the exploratory ones, the pattern says something about what people chose to preregister once they had tried the alternatives, which I think is worth a conversation. [advance] If anything misbehaves, raise your hand and work down the list on the cheatsheet. If your machine has given up altogether, your specification is one row of the curve, which the download button on the Specification curve page serves with its t and its degrees of freedom, and I will help you submit it by hand, so that everybody has a dot on the chart.
:::
